sections.body: A synthesis page could compare how compiler optimization systems use empirical evidence from workloads, profiles, or training data rather than static heuristics alone.
sections.heading: Section 1

sections.body: Aestimo provides the sharpest warning: training inputs change FDO decisions and measured performance, workload-wide evaluation is needed, and single-input evaluation can be unreliable. Profile-guided classic optimization and machine-learning compilation make related evidence-based arguments, but with different mechanisms: hot-path execution profiles and learned models trained from representative program data.
sections.heading: Section 2

sections.body: The section should preserve the ambiguity that better feedback is not automatically better performance, since the bzip2 resubstitution result did not reliably predict the fastest FDO binary.
